corrected_start_analysis.conclusion: Executable routine ends with RTS at PRG 259407. The immediately following bytes at 259408 and 259418 are two valid 10-byte records. The previous 259428 start omitted them. Correct contiguous span is 64 records from 259408 through 260047.

corrections: Previous 62-record start at 259428 was too late by 20 bytes. Correct structural span is 64 records starting at 259408.

deep_batch_4.mapper71_mapping_note: For the 256 KiB PRG image, fixed-bank CPU addresses $C000-$FFFF correspond to the final 16 KiB PRG bank (file PRG offsets 245760..262143). Therefore table PRG offset 259408 maps to CPU $F550; previous $F564 was record index 2, not the table start.
deep_batch_4.important_correction: Earlier analysis treated $F564 as the table base. After restoring the two leading records, the structural base is $F550. $F564 is 20 bytes into the table.

exhaustive_operand_scan.warning: Most hits are in switchable banks/data and cannot be called executed references without bank/control-flow proof.

deep_batch_4.next_required_proof: Disassemble the final fixed bank from known vectors/control-flow roots, then retain only reachable instructions referencing $F550-$F7CF.

control_flow_batch.conclusion: Recursive control-flow trace from NMI/RESET/IRQ in the fixed bank reaches the routine ending at F54F and does not fall through into F550 table data. No reachable direct absolute instruction in this conservative trace references F550-F7CF. Table access is therefore likely indirect/indexed through RAM/pointer state or from switchable-bank code; semantics remain unassigned.
control_flow_batch.caveat: Trace follows official 6502 lengths, direct JSR/JMP and relative branches in the fixed bank; indirect JMP targets and mapper-selected switchable-bank execution require separate state-aware analysis.

fixed_bank_search.note: The two reachable-looking A9 #$50 sites store $50 into $A3 but are followed by unrelated constants ($1A/$12 into $93), so they are not evidence of constructing pointer $F550.

indirect_access_batch.inference: No literal $F550 pointer construction was found in the fixed bank. Combined with zero reachable direct absolute references, access is not a simple fixed-bank absolute/literal-base load. Next target is switchable-bank code and RAM pointer provenance.
indirect_access_batch.evidence_level: byte-search plus fixed-bank context; no field semantics assigned

mapper_write_batch.finding: The fixed bank contains a systematic family of immediate-value stores into C00A..C017-like addresses. This is stronger evidence of a bank/trampoline mechanism than treating arbitrary >=8000 stores as mapper writes. Bank value 13 is explicitly present in the family (A9 0D / STA C017 at about EF6C).
mapper_write_batch.caution: The exact hardware/software role of these C00x addresses is not yet assigned; they may be RAM-backed bank-call state/trampoline data rather than direct mapper registers.
mapper_write_batch.bank13_status: Selection/value 13 is now evidenced in reachable fixed-bank neighborhood, but reachability from that mechanism to bank13 candidate AA66 still needs instruction-level tracing.

bank13_trace_from_b265.key_finding: The proven bank-13 entry immediately performs indexed-indirect data reads through zero-page pointer $12/$13. This supplies a concrete mechanism by which fixed-bank data can be consumed without any literal F550 operand in the bank-13 code.
bank13_trace_from_b265.implication: The next decisive target is provenance of zero-page $12/$13 at the EF6C -> B265 call site. If it resolves to F550 (or an offset within F550-F7CF), table access and record semantics can be traced from real code.

b265_postmatch.structural_result: B312/B3E5/B4B8/B58B are four aligned 211-byte columns (210 entries plus boundary/terminator spacing) indexed by the same Y. The matched B312 index selects three companion values.
b265_postmatch.inference: The data is a structure-of-arrays object/placement table. B3E5 and B4B8 participate in 16-bit subtraction against RAM $03BB/$03BC, strongly suggesting a 16-bit position/address-like quantity, but exact semantics are not yet named.
b265_postmatch.next: Extract all four columns for 210 entries and correlate B3E5/B4B8/B58B with runtime variables and the 64-record F550 table.

bank13_four_columns.finding: All four columns contain exactly 210 payload bytes followed by FF at aligned boundaries. This proves a 210-row four-column data structure indexed by the same Y.
bank13_four_columns.arithmetic: B3E5,Y is low byte and B4B8,Y participates as high byte in SEC/SBC against 03BB/03BC, so columns 1+2 form a 16-bit little-endian quantity in the executed code.
bank13_four_columns.caution: The meaning of that 16-bit quantity and the fourth column is still intentionally unnamed.

bank13_16bit_column_analysis.executed_operation: SEC; LDA low[Y]; SBC $03BB; STA $1E; LDA high[Y]; SBC $03BC
bank13_16bit_column_analysis.result: The code computes value16 - word($03BB,$03BC). Low-byte result is stored in $1E; high-byte result remains in A and is tested with BNE.
bank13_16bit_column_analysis.implication: The branch tests whether the high byte of the signed/modular 16-bit difference is zero. Only values whose difference from $03BB/$03BC lies in 0..255 continue to the B58B[Y] path.
bank13_16bit_column_analysis.fourth_column: B58B[Y] is then loaded and transferred to Y before JSR $1F84.
bank13_16bit_column_analysis.caution: This proves a range/window comparison against a 16-bit runtime base, but does not yet identify the physical meaning of either quantity.

runtime_base_03bb_03bc.derivation: $03BC is initialized to 0. $03BB starts as the low 3 bits of RAM $11, then is incremented by a value computed through repeated ASL/ROL of $03BC and arithmetic using $4E/$4F.
runtime_base_03bb_03bc.important_result: $03BB/$03BC is not an arbitrary pointer loaded from ROM. It is a runtime-computed 16-bit quantity.
runtime_base_03bb_03bc.next: Trace RAM $4E/$4F and $11 feeding routine 866B to identify the physical/gameplay meaning of the runtime base.

runtime_base_inputs.input_11: low three bits are copied into low byte of $03BB before further arithmetic
runtime_base_inputs.input_4e_4f: used as a 16-bit runtime operand during the shift/add sequence that builds $03BB/$03BC
runtime_base_inputs.constraint: Because only $11&7 seeds the low bits while $4E/$4F drives the larger-scale term, the computed base has a coarse component from $4E/$4F plus a 0..7 fine component from $11.
runtime_base_inputs.consequence_for_bank13: The 210-entry value16 column is compared against this coarse+fine runtime base; this is consistent with spatial/window indexing but is not sufficient to name coordinates.

input_writer_batch.methodology: Search reachable decoded code for direct zero-page stores and register stores to these addresses, then group by routine/call context rather than treating raw byte matches as instructions.

findings.$93: Already observed as comparison key in bank13 B265; treat as runtime group key only.
findings.$11: Feeds only its low three bits into the 03BB/03BC base builder at 8670.
findings.$4E/$4F: Form the coarse 16-bit input used by the base-building arithmetic.
findings.relation: The code path uses $93 as a categorical selector and 03BB/03BC as a separate numeric window base; these are independent selection dimensions.

input_writer_batch.semantic_constraint: Do not collapse $93 and the computed base into a single room/position identifier. The executed code clearly performs a two-stage selection: group match first, numeric-window test second.

fixed_bank_writer_evidence.notable_initialization: CBD3-CBDC clears $4E, $11 and $4F together (and nearby state), showing these variables belong to mutable runtime state rather than ROM pointers.
fixed_bank_writer_evidence.notable_93: E1xx/E2xx contains many immediate assignments to $93, including values 0x1F,0x1D,0x13,0x2E,0x18,0x1E,0x2C,0x22. This supports $93 as an explicit categorical/state value.
